subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining browser-tool slice should OpenClaw sponsor first from this field report: state/readiness signals, model-facing batch schema/docs, CDP element inspection, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker signaling, or post-fill verification?
rationale: Current main already shipped part of the request, but the remaining work changes model-facing browser API behavior and agent state semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Prioritize state/readiness signals
options.body: Split stale-ref hints, snapshot readiness, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker detection, and action-result diffs into focused maintainer-owned issues before implementation.

options.title: Advertise batch first
options.body: Expose and document the existing managed-browser batch path in the model-facing schema before tackling the broader state-signal work.

options.title: Close after partial fixes
options.body: Treat selector support, selector waits, ARIA refs, click delay, and lower-level batch execution as enough and decline the remaining umbrella requests for now.

recommendation.title: Prioritize state/readiness signals
recommendation.body: Split stale-ref hints, snapshot readiness, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker detection, and action-result diffs into focused maintainer-owned issues before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior partial browser action fix and have the clearest recent history on selector and batch action contracts.
